We are looking for a Battery Systems Engineer to lead the design, development, and validation of advanced low-voltage battery packs. In this role, you will be responsible for battery pack architecture, mechanical integration, thermal management, cell evaluation, electrochemical testing, and safety compliance. Working closely with cross-functional teams and external suppliers, you will drive projects from concept development through prototyping, testing, and production release, ensuring high-performance, reliable, and safe energy storage solutions.

- Pack design & mechanical integration: Design low-voltage battery packs, enclosures, cell modules, busbars and interconnects in CAD — from first concept through to release-ready drawings and BOMs.

- Thermal & structural layout: Develop thermal management concepts and validate them against mechanical loads, vibration and shock requirements of the target application.

- Cell selection & benchmarking: Evaluate and qualify cells from different suppliers; build the data basis for design decisions on energy density, power capability, cycle life and cost.

- Electrochemical testing: Plan, run and evaluate cell and module tests — capacity and rate characterisation, EIS, ageing and cycle-life campaigns, thermal characterisation — and derive design conclusions from the results.

- Test infrastructure: Set up and maintain test benches, fixtures and measurement chains; build repeatable test procedures and keep the data properly documented and traceable.

- Prototyping & validation: Build and instrument prototype packs, run the validation programme, and feed findings back into the next design iteration.

- Safety & standards: Support hazard and risk assessments, define protection concepts (fusing, isolation, venting, propagation resistance) and prepare packs for the relevant transport and product standards (e.g. UN 38.3, IEC 62133).

- Interface management: Coordinate technically with mechanics, electronics/BMS, manufacturing and purchasing, and act as the technical counterpart to external cell and component suppliers.

- Completed degree in engineering or natural sciences — electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, chemistry, physics or materials science.

- Roughly 3–5 years of hands-on experience in battery development, ideally with low-voltage packs for mobile or embedded applications.

- Solid understanding of lithium-ion cell chemistry and electrochemistry, cell-to-pack architecture and thermal behavior.

- Confident with CAD (e.g. Siemens NX, SolidWorks or CATIA); experience with design for manufacturing and joining technologies for cell contacting (welding, bonding) is a plus.

- Solid understanding of state estimation, balancing, thermal control and their interaction with pack hardware

- Practical experience with cell cyclers, climate chambers, EIS, data acquisition and general lab measurement technique is a plus.

- Comfortable evaluating test data with Python or MATLAB; basic familiarity with thermal or electrical simulation is welcome.

- Working knowledge of the safety, testing and transport standards relevant to lithium-ion batteries.

- Analytical, structured way of working, hands-on mentality in the lab, and the ability to work across disciplines in a small, fast-moving team.
